entries.title: Applying a sync conflict copy installs the exact committed merge and returns the journal to ordinary conflict-free editing
entries.notes: Martin's 2026-08-22 Direct Files tests exposed a continuing incomplete handoff: the pre-merge editor could remain installed; resolving today's journal could omit that mutation-held day; sticky notices could outlive the object; a winner-file watcher event declined during mutation ownership remained parked until the next edit and then looked divergent; an older inventory refresh could republish an already-resolved conflict; and a same-content resolution could lose its disk baseline so the next edit reopened Concord. The correction contract requires event-independent discovery, a quiescent exact-DTO handoff, atomic journal-feed publication, immediate replay when explicit ownership releases, newest-generation inventory publication, notification retirement, and a successful ordinary post-resolution edit after both changed-content and same-content handoffs.

entries.title: Managed save conflicts retain the editor draft and offer a revision-bound Keep mine or Use current choice
entries.notes: Necessity gate proven: the managed native gateway rejected every force before actor invocation and mapped stale saves to a permanent toast, so the retained draft had no in-app authoring path. The covered path observes the exact pinned managed path and revision without loading it into the editor, binds Keep mine to that observation, serializes the replacement through one actor turn, re-conflicts after a second accepted change, recreates remotely deleted retained blocks under fresh durable IDs, and disables replacement for missing, renamed, ambiguous, or otherwise unobservable owners. A baseRev-null draft that loses a concurrent create observes the winner independently by logical name and kind, then resolves against that exact winner path and revision. Use current does not reload or discard the retained draft until the user explicitly selects it.

Fixed: query_plan::execute_blocks builds a global bounded-heap top-k with real per-block relevance (match-class > word-boundary > earlier-offset > shorter-text > fewer-occurrences, deterministic tie-break by (page rel_path, in-page index) — bare traversal index was nondeterministic because walk_page_files reads fs::read_dir unsorted; regression block_search_topk_ties_sort_rel_path_with_reversed_page_snapshot forces a reversed page snapshot); OG caps adopted (inline pages 100 / block-refs 20; Ctrl+K 100/100 ranked pool, existing chunked presentation); autocomplete fold NFKC->NFC to match #137/backend. Fail-before proven (best block on last page survives + ranks ahead of weaker earlier matches; NFC-vs-NFKC ordering). Manager-reviewed block top-k + green (tine-core 455, autocomplete 50, component 20); not separately adversarially verified (search-ordering, lower risk than #137).

entries.title: Settings panel scrolls on narrow/mobile viewports so every setting is reachable

entries.title: Accepting a page/block-ref completion while editing inside an existing ref rewrites the whole ref, leaving no stray closing bracket (Logseq parity)
entries.notes: GH #199. Editing inside an already-closed [[word]] (e.g. autopaired [[second]], arrow-left, type 'first ' -> [[first |second]]) and accepting a completion left a stray ]] ([[first]]second]]) because Block.tsx replaceTrigger only swallowed the closing pair when it sat IMMEDIATELY at the caret (ref.value.slice(t.end,t.end+2)===pair). OG-verified (og@6e7afa8, findings in tine-agents specs notes): OG's query range is [[->caret (matches Tine's detectTrigger, unchanged), but on accept OG scans forward from the caret to the ref's closer (:end-pattern ]]), strips it (postfix-fn) and rewrites the whole region. Fix: new pure refCompletionEnd(value,end,insertedText) in autocomplete.ts scans forward on the CURRENT LINE for the closer matching the completion's suffix (]]/))/}}), returning just past it or the caret when none ahead; replaceTrigger now uses it. Covers page AND block refs (same latent defect) and the latent end-caret ]]]] doubling. Not a regression: latent since the autocomplete feature shipped (e54ad36e, 2026-06-14). Fail-before proven (pre-fix immediate-only range yields [[first]]second]]); 7 unit cases (mid/end/unclosed/block/line-bounded/non-ref/reporter-integration); Block.referenceAuthoring + tagAutocomplete + selectionWrap render tests still green (wiring regression guard). Delegated to gpt-5.6-terra (xhigh), manager-reviewed + gates run. Real-app editor confirmation pending on next deploy (pure-logic fix, proportionate).

entries.notes: OG-parity catalogue pick (og-parity.assets-pdf-media.raw-remote-image-url, LIVE-BACKLOG s9). Tine renderLink (src/render/inline.tsx) rendered media only when the lsdoc node had image:true (![](url) syntax); a BARE https://host/pic.jpg link fell through to a plain <a class=external-link> (pre-fix). Fix: when !s.image AND s.full (raw source = OG full_text) starts with http(s):// AND mediaKind(dest)!=null, route to AssetImage (image) / MediaEmbed (video/audio) -- the components the s.image branch already uses. Discriminator on s.full (not label emptiness) is byte-faithful to OG: a labeled [text](x.png) has full '[text](x.png)' (not http-prefixed) and STAYS a link. Pure render change, no write path. Extension set = Tine's canonical mediaKind (media.ts) rather than OG's literal list (Tine adds avif/m4v/oga/opus; lacks ico) -- an intentional harmless presentation-heuristic difference, noted per AGENTS parity doctrine. Fail-before proven (manager-run).

entries.title: Delete/Backspace over a rendered (not-editing) block text selection deletes that text, matching OG contenteditable
entries.notes: Martin internal report: selecting block text and pressing Delete/Backspace sometimes does nothing, seemingly speed-dependent. Real-app matrix (27 cases, WebKitGTK) showed editor selections always delete; the dead keypress is a RENDERED-view (not-editing) text selection — Tine separates rendered view from textarea, the drag is treated as text selection not a click-to-edit, and Delete reaches no editor (selection stays, nothing changes). Fix: window-capture Delete/Backspace with a non-collapsed selection inside one block's rendered wrapper maps endpoints to source offsets (render/spans.ts) and splices visible text via the normal setRaw path (undo, dirty), then opens the editor at the join point. Conservative no-ops: cross-block selections, selections inside atomic constructs (links/chips — coarse spans snap to the same edge), annotation/calc blocks, read-only pages, blocks already being edited, modals open, unmapped endpoints. Side observation (untouched): WebKit smart-delete on native double-click word selections eats one trailing space uniformly (fast and slow).

entries.title: The bundled app scripts parse and run on pre-16.4 Safari/WKWebView (macOS 12) instead of dying at startup with an invalid-regex SyntaxError and a white screen
entries.notes: GH #256. Debug log showed Safari's parse-time 'invalid group specifier name' error: src/mock.ts shipped the bundle's only regex lookbehind in the modulepreloaded app chunk. Guard test greps all src sources for lookbehind (failed on mock.ts:65 pre-fix); tagsOf now uses a prefix-capture group with identical behavior (old-vs-new output compared on 10 samples). Real macOS 12 WKWebView confirmation not possible in this environment. REVIEW CORRECTION (manager, integration): the first fix replaced the negative lookbehind with a leading capture group `(^|[^\[])#...`, which READS as equivalent but CONSUMES the preceding character, so with a global regex a tag written immediately after another one had nothing left to match its prefix against and was silently dropped -- `#a#b` yielded only `a`, and `#[[x]]#y` only `x`, in 4 of 13 probed inputs. The lookbehind is zero-width; the replacement must be too. Corrected to check the preceding character AFTER the match, which keeps the test zero-width, and src/mockTags.test.ts now calls the real tagsOf (not a copy of its regex) and fails against the first fix.

entries.title: In-page find (Ctrl+F) reveal centers the exact occurrence, not merely its block, when the block is taller than the viewport
entries.notes: GH #253. Matches were already tracked per-occurrence and highlighted; only the reveal scrolled the whole block to center. revealInPageFindMatch now resolves the active occurrence's Range rect (same ordinal as the highlight layer) and adjusts the nearest vertical scroller to center it, falling back to the coarse block scroll when no DOM-text range exists (edit-mode textarea). WebKitGTK scroll behavior not runtime-verified here; jsdom test with stubbed range rects proves the semantic scroll delta (fail-before: scrollTop stayed 0 pre-fix). REVIEW CORRECTION (manager, integration): nearestVerticalScroller accepted any ancestor with overflow-y auto/scroll, including one that does not actually overflow. Adjusting such an element's scrollTop is a no-op, and the function still reported success, so the caller skipped its block-level scrollIntoView fallback and the occurrence stayed off-screen -- strictly worse than the behaviour this change replaced. It now requires scrollHeight > clientHeight; the existing jsdom fixture had to start modelling a scroller that really can scroll. KNOWN COVERAGE GAP: a regression test for the non-scrolling-ancestor branch was attempted and withdrawn -- revealInPageFindMatch did not reach the scroll step under that jsdom fixture and chasing it was harness work, not product work (AGENTS.md economy rule). The guard is reasoned from the DOM contract and is not covered by a test.

entries.title: Windows update checks use the native network trust path and require a separate install confirmation
entries.notes: GH #241. The earlier catch fix exposed the reporter's concrete failure: Tauri's default rustls updater transport could not send the latest.json request on their otherwise-online Windows 11 installation, before manifest parsing, signature verification, download, or installation. Windows updater builds now use reqwest native-tls/Schannel so the request follows the OS-native certificate and network trust path; Linux/macOS retain the shipped rustls path. Cargo feature-tree evidence proves Windows selects native-tls and Linux selects rustls-tls; physical reporter confirmation remains necessary. The explicit Check for updates action no longer installs by itself: it reports availability and presents a separate sticky Install update action. Installer failures remain logged and visible, with the releases page as fallback.

entries.title: Enter and multiline paste inside a $$ … $$ environment keep the block together instead of splitting it
entries.notes: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM OG, approved by Martin 2026-08-09. OG's Enter dwim (frontend/util/thingatpt.cljs admonition&src-at-point) recognises only ``` and #+BEGIN_, so OG also splits the bullet and breaks the environment; the reporter is asking for an improvement, not restored parity. The v0.6.92 Enter fix was too narrow: the reporter's post-release follow-up proved that pasting LaTeX containing a blank line into the same environment still segmented it into outline blocks. The shared syntax-sensitive editor decision now uses caretInDisplayMath for paste as well as Enter, including selection replacement; ordinary blank-line prose still segments normally. The parser, on-disk bytes and property classification remain untouched. Necessity gate proven: the exact reporter paste tests fail before the paste predicate is widened.

entries.title: Clicking a task marker label uses Logseq's open-state toggle and never removes DONE
entries.notes: OG source at 6e7afa8eb separates marker-switch (components/block.cljs:1861) from keyboard cycle-marker-state (util/marker.cljs:40): label clicks toggle TODO/DOING and LATER/NOW, while DONE is not clickable; keyboard cycling may still reach DONE and then remove the marker. Tine had wired both block and Sheet label clicks to its keyboard cycle, so clicking DONE silently removed completion. The click helper is now separate, preserves the existing logbook transition machinery, and is shared by ordinary blocks and Sheet state cells. Keyboard and checkbox behavior are unchanged. The reporter confirmed this exact OG behavior and accepted it.

entries.title: Generic custom.css image sizing does not constrain the full-screen lightbox
entries.notes: Graph custom.css intentionally loads after Tine's stylesheet, so a generic `img { width: 320px; height: auto }` thumbnail rule also constrained `.lightbox-img`. The lightbox now owns its geometry through the more-specific `.lightbox-overlay > img.lightbox-img` rule with auto width/height, viewport maxima and object-fit contain. A later generic img rule remains effective for inline thumbnails but loses only on the dedicated lightbox surface; users can still target `.lightbox-img` explicitly if desired.

entries.title: Native page selections exclude Add block and reference-section UI labels
entries.notes: The reporter's concrete copied suffixes are UI labels, not page content: `+ Add block`, `Linked References`, and `Unlinked References`. The trailing target and every references header now opt out of native selection in both standard and WebKit-prefixed CSS, so mouse/touch selection can cross the page without copying application chrome. This deliberately does not attempt nonstandard region-containment semantics; actual reference block content remains selectable.

entries.title: Native page selections exclude page action control labels (carry-over buttons, tag-table toggle, guide copy, ⋯ trigger)
entries.notes: Internal report (Martin, 2026-08-25): texts of page action controls such as the journal carry-over buttons became part of ordinary dragged text selections. The title-row controls — carry-over buttons, tag-table toggle, guide copy button and the ⋯ page-actions trigger — now opt out of native selection in both standard and WebKit-prefixed CSS while remaining ordinary activatable buttons (pointer events and keyboard focus are untouched; the icon-only favorite star contributes no selection text and is intentionally out of scope). Page and block content remains selectable.

entries.title: Copy / export as… offers an explicit preserve-Markdown/Org content choice next to cleaned plain text
entries.notes: Current-state preflight: the reporter's v0.6.93 already contained the Content choice (Rendered cleaned / Source preserved, shipped 2026-07-02), but nothing on the modal said 'Markdown' or 'plain text', so the preserve option was undiscoverable — the harm is the invisible choice, while the transformation already preserved the source syntax. The Content buttons now name the outcome: Plain text (cleaned, default retained) and Markdown — format-aware, so an Org forest offers Org — with hints echoing the issue's preserve/clean wording; the two moot-toggle tooltips use the same vocabulary. Modal render tests prove both directions at the block entry point (explicit labels present; preserve keeps **bold**, [[links]], property lines, ==highlight==; default cleans them), the page entry point shares the one modal (ContextMenu.test.tsx covers both routings), and pure exportText tests pin verbatim source syntax inside the requested exported outline for representative inline formatting, nested blocks, and Org emphasis/drawers.

entries.title: Navigating to a block nested inside collapsed parents expands its ancestors, scrolls to it and highlights it
entries.notes: openPageAtBlock polled the DOM for .ls-block[data-block-id] up to 20x50ms, but Block.tsx renders no children for a collapsed parent, so a Ctrl+Shift+K block result inside a collapsed subtree could never match and the poll timed out silently. store.expandAncestors expands the target's own ancestor chain (not unrelated collapsed blocks) as ONE undo step, persisting collapsed:: exactly as a manual expand does. Necessity gate proven: two of the three tests fail on the pre-fix tree. Reporter supplied an AI-written root cause; it was independently confirmed against router.ts:596 and Block.tsx:577 before implementing.

entries.title: Linked and Unlinked References keep the user's expand/collapse choice when the page subtree re-renders
entries.notes: Reported on a >5,000-page graph: a page with ~173 linked references collapsed its own section while scrolling or expanding a group, while ~48 references behaved. The flag was a component-local signal, so ANY remount of the page subtree reset it, and OG_REFERENCE_COLLAPSE_THRESHOLD=100 makes 'reset' mean collapsed — which is precisely the 48-fine/173-broken split. Moving the state to src/referenceSectionState.ts makes the symptom impossible whatever causes the remount, which is what the reporter asked for ('stay in current existing state no matter what'). Memory-only: OG's collapse-above-100 default still applies on a fresh start, and resetStore clears it on graph switch. NOT YET REPRODUCED on a real large graph — the remount trigger (suspected Page.tsx pagesToRender() going transiently empty) is unconfirmed; keep reported until a large-graph user or the Direct Files perf audit confirms.

entries.title: Ctrl+O opens the page at the caret, Ctrl+Shift+O opens it in the sidebar
entries.notes: OG parity gap: OG binds :editor/follow-link to mod+o and :editor/open-link-in-sidebar to mod+shift+o (frontend/modules/shortcut/config.cljs:214/:217); Tine had no mod+o at all. The 'which link' rule is transcribed from OG's thingatpt.cljs extract-nearest-link-from-text, including its surprising part: OG collects EVERY candidate in the block and picks the one nearest the caret, so a caret anywhere in a block with one link still follows it. URLs are included for follow and deliberately excluded for the sidebar, matching OG's two call sites. Block refs are best-effort: a bare ((uuid)) in raw text carries no page, so a block outside the loaded working set is not found - the same give-up OG's open-link-in-sidebar! does when db/get-page misses. FAIL-BEFORE is an absence (no mod+o binding existed), verified by grep.

entries.title: Android Back never exits after an unverified managed shutdown and remains owned before JavaScript is ready
entries.notes: An Android AppPlugin listener could fall back to WebView history or activity finish before JavaScript subscribed, while the process-wide managed shutdown helper collapsed terminal and safe outcomes and could exit after a terminal runtime. The repair introduces a native SafeBack owner that consumes all Back events unless its own listener is ready, and a typed process preparation result: only Safe may exit; Refused reopens the editor only when no managed slot was verified; Partial or an unknown transport result remains shielded and retries native preparation alone. JS tests cover listener lifecycle and the zero-progress/partial/unknown retry matrix; Rust tests cover sorted stop-at-first-refusal aggregation, terminal rejection and Safe retry. Physical Android compilation and hardware Back remain hosted-CI/device gates.

entries.title: Managed-storage runtime status, progress and failure reasons update the app and open Storage & sync panel for the current graph only
entries.notes: Confirmed UI audit H1 at dc82d0c4: watcher.rs emitted sparse-v2-status, sparse-v2-tick and sparse-v2-error, but the frontend subscribed only to sparse-v2-changed. The Settings panel therefore retained its open-time status snapshot and the runtime's explicit failure reason was invisible. A single app-owned typed bridge now updates both surfaces, preserves the native reason text, and accepts an event only when its binding generation matches the currently bound graph. Direct-file managed-sync-error and graph-watch-error listeners remain unchanged.

entries.title: A graph open that stalls or fails reports its phase and offers retry, another graph, copied details, and an escape back to Direct Files
entries.notes: Before this cycle neither src/startupRecovery.ts nor src/components/StartupRecovery.tsx existed (both are added against v0.6.92), so a stalled open painted nothing and offered no action; that is the literal pre-state rather than a reconstructed one. The overlay appears only after STARTUP_PROGRESS_VISIBLE_MS so an ordinary fast open still shows nothing, becomes role=alertdialog on recovery, and states that no managed-storage data has been discarded. The Return-to-Direct-Files action is gated on a real native lookup authority token (nativeAttempt > 0), so it is never offered for a graph that was never enrolled. Copy details uses the resilient clipboard transport because recovery must not depend exclusively on the native invoke bridge it is diagnosing. Declining recovery resumes the open rather than stranding the app. Fail-before is reconstructed from the superseded source at v0.6.92, not from a red run executed at release time.

entries.title: Indent, outdent and repeated moves on a multi-block selection apply as one shared-store command and one undo unit
entries.notes: F1 indent/outdent previously removed and reinserted each selected root separately; roots drawn from different original sibling arrays are now removed once and inserted in visible order. F2 collapses a run of Up/Down moves into one command family that closes on idle, a three-second maximum, a changed selected-root set, an Undo or Redo, an unrelated edit, or a page reload, so one Undo reverses the move rather than one block of it. Read-only refusals are preserved exactly: a feed-spanning selection containing a read-only day is refused and dirties neither page, and a writable feed-spanning outdent leaves the other day byte-identical and clean. Zoom-scope containment is asserted on both operations. Fail-before is reconstructed from the superseded source at v0.6.92, not from a red run executed at release time.

entries.title: Pasting many blocks with preserved IDs makes one loaded-document identity pass instead of one per candidate
entries.notes: The superseded per-id predicate rescanned every loaded key and every loaded raw for each incoming identity, so cost grew with candidates times page size. The batched helper is asserted through an explicit work receipt (src/clipboardWorkProbe.ts): 200+ preserved-ID paste and redo candidates each record exactly one loaded_identity_pass, and incoming_identity_ids_checked stays fixed as the loaded document grows. Fail-closed behaviour is unchanged and independently asserted: an internally duplicated moved payload is rejected before the loaded document is consulted, and both the Markdown id:: and Org :id: raw forms are still matched without requiring an Org drawer. Fail-before is reconstructed from the superseded source at v0.6.92, not from a red run executed at release time.

entries.title: Property autocomplete remains usable when authored entirely from the keyboard
entries.notes: OG moves the caret before a line-opening :: delimiter and searches the property name to its left. Tine previously left the caret after ::, so the first name character produced malformed ::a text, closed the popup, and could surface repeated backend error notifications. Coverage exercises the real input-event lifecycle: :: moves the caret left; typed characters filter without closing; Create is discoverable at the top; selection enters value search; a directly authored key:: followed by space also enters value search; and comma starts a new value search with already-authored values excluded. Facet lookup failure is contained to the optional autocomplete surface and cannot reject the editor input event.

entries.title: Dragging a block into the deep target zone makes it a child of that block
entries.notes: Tine's pointer drag implementation exposed only before/after sibling targets, so Windows was not exceptional: no platform could express OG's nested drop. OG 6e7afa8eb chooses :nested when the pointer is more than 50px inside the target block and moves the dragged roots under that target. The shared pointer path now uses that same intent threshold and a distinct child indicator. The target-relative store transaction accepts child placement for one or many normalized selected roots, appends them after existing children, preserves subtrees, page reassignment and order-list inheritance, rejects self/descendant cycles through the existing plan, and remains one undo/redo unit. Cross-page managed moves transmit the equivalent child placement to the storage actor.

entries.title: Custom CSS can enable Inter OpenType stylistic sets and character variants
entries.notes: The custom CSS property itself reached the computed style correctly; the bundled @fontsource/inter per-script static subsets lacked ss02 and every other Inter stylistic set. Tine now ships the audited full upstream Inter 4.1 variable faces under the same public Inter family name, preserving existing themes and user CSS while restoring ss01-ss08 and cv01-cv14. The regression pins both upstream font hashes and verifies the public family and variable-weight declarations; the production build separately proves Vite emits both faces.

entries.title: The release E2E distinguishes undelivered native ArrowDown input from broken page-header traversal
entries.notes: Release run 31569006329 observed no keydown witness despite the expected header activeElement; the unchanged candidate passed the rerun and six focused repetitions. The journey now uses a real pointer action to transfer native focus, proves document focus/editor/caret readiness, and retries locally only when no key witness arrives. The suite runner may retry that isolated scenario once on the explicit E2E_NATIVE_INPUT_UNDELIVERED receipt. An unmodified ArrowDown witnessed on the expected header but failing to enter the first body block remains an immediate blocking product failure.

entries.title: The release E2E distinguishes an unready GTK upload chooser from an upload product failure
entries.notes: The unchanged v0.6.93 candidate passed the same literal upload journey twice and failed once after a blind chooser activation/type/120ms sequence. The harness already launches Openbox, so a missing window manager was not the current cause. It now proves the chooser is visible and EWMH-active, submits the absolute path, observes closure, and only reactivates/sends Open while the chooser remains visibly mapped. The suite runner may retry the isolated scenario once only on E2E_NATIVE_CHOOSER_INPUT_UNDELIVERED. If the chooser closes but the graph asset or Markdown write is absent, the existing blocking product assertion remains unchanged.

entries.title: The release E2E waits for semantic block-embed content before interacting with it
entries.notes: The v0.6.92 journey clicked as soon as embed macro roots existed, while cross-page descendants populated asynchronously; adding an unrelated await moved the failure between disclosure and arrow/delete. The semantic readiness repair then exposed a deterministic product defect: multiple visible refs/embeds to the same initially unloaded page raced activation; one loaded the exact page, while siblings treated their expected stale-install refusal as permanent failure and stayed shallow. LiveRefGroup now rechecks the exact loaded kind/path after every installation attempt, so a sibling winner hydrates all groups while a different page/path remains refused. A render regression forces two concurrent activation promises and proves both descendants render with one retained activation. The release journey waits for exactly the identities/content/disclosure controls it will operate on, asserts no timing or pixels, and is restored to stable blocking coverage.

entries.title: Setting up or joining managed sync reopens the actor retired by the enrollment cut before reporting success
entries.notes: The real two-device journey reached healthy local activation, then the first explicit share cut stopped its actor by design and the Tauri command immediately queried that retired handle, returning sync actor is unavailable. Share and already-managed join now reopen the durable post-enrollment runtime, prove its ordinary page inventory/load boundary, and publish a new exact-generation graph slot before returning success. That repair exposed a second product defect: a bounded watcher scan could acknowledge one epoch while newer observations remained pending, but an AdmittedNoop/Complete tick scheduled no continuation and a quiet graph supplied no new inotify edge. The watcher now consults the actor's post-tick pending bit, drains all retained epochs without a timer guess, and still leaves a truly quiet actor asleep. The source regressions pin cut -> reopen -> exact publish ordering and pending-epoch continuation; the real two-device journey remains the release-blocking semantic proof.

entries.title: A peer edit delivered into managed storage becomes visible without waiting for an unrelated filesystem event
entries.notes: The two-device journey delivered device B's edit into device A's graph-local provider tree while device A was stopped. On reopen, device A discovered the delivery (provider_pending=3) while its watcher was idle (pending=false, latest_enqueue=2, acknowledged=2), and the peer edit never appeared. The Tauri sparse scheduler decided continuation from the tick result plus the actor's watcher pending bit only, so a tick that settled a watcher epoch read as a quiet graph and cleared the retry schedule; a quiet graph produces no further inotify edge for bytes another device wrote, so the delivered work was stranded forever. The actor now publishes provider_runnable alongside provider_pending - the exact predicate tick consults, not the broad inventory that legitimately never reaches zero while durable publication intents remain - and the scheduler continues while SyncRuntimeStatusSnapshot::has_runnable_work() is true. A tick that reports Idle while still naming runnable provider work is paced by the ordinary backoff schedule instead of the progress cadence, so a blocked causal dependency cannot become a poll loop, and a genuinely quiet actor still arms no timer at all. Source regressions pin arrival across the delivery/reopen cut, arrival to a running receiver, a multi-item drain to zero with interleaved page reads, and the idle direction; the real two-device journey remains the release-blocking semantic proof.

entries.title: A peer edit that lands in managed SQLite always reaches the Markdown file, even when a local external edit is admitted in the same window
entries.notes: On a running receiving device, an inbound provider batch could be applied to SQLite while its Markdown file was never written. The receiver-local projection decided whether a delivered foreign intent was still the live authority by comparing the intent's post-frontier with the page's WHOLE current merged frontier. An ordinary local external admission landing in the same window commits its own batch, which advances the shared page-catalog document, so the delivered intent stopped matching a page it never touched; the intent was then treated as superseded historical evidence and dropped. Nothing else owned that path, so the page existed in ListPages at the right path with no file on disk, clean_shutdown still returned Safe, and a reopen with a full re-drive never repaired it - durable data-visibility loss, since Markdown is the interchange truth for Direct Files parity and for every external tool. A receiver that cannot prove the delivered intent is still current now projects the page's CURRENT accepted state instead of skipping it (idempotent: a genuinely superseded page renders to the bytes already on disk), projects at the path the accepted state names rather than the intent's stale one, and retains the obligation as a published continuation when neither the intent nor the current state can be authorized. Source regressions pin creates, edits and cross-page moves under that interleaving, each with a Safe shutdown and a clean reopen. NOT covered here: provider-delivered DELETES and RENAMES never converge on the clean runtime at all - with or without the interleaving - because the receiver-local tombstone authorization still requires the retired pre-0.7 durable endpoint history store; that is a separate open defect.

entries.title: The Android Back gesture reaches Tine's rungs and closes the Settings modal instead of silently stepping WebView history
entries.notes: Reported internally by Martin: with the Settings modal open, the hardware Back gesture did not close it. The frontend rungs were never at fault - dispatchAndroidBack, the transient registry and Settings' three-rung dismiss all behave correctly in the real app composition, which is why the defect survived. androidx's OnBackPressedDispatcher hands a gesture to the LAST-ADDED enabled callback, and Tauri's core AppPlugin adds its own from its Kotlin constructor, which runs on the Rust startup thread tao spawns inside Rust.create() - after MainActivity.onCreate has already returned. AppPlugin therefore sat ABOVE Tine's SafeBack owner, took its no-listener branch (Tine registers android-safe-back on its own plugin, never back-button on Tauri's) and answered Back with WebView.goBack() whenever the WebView had history. The mobile router pushes one history entry per navigation, so after the user's first navigation every Back popped a route BEHIND whatever was on screen and no rung ever ran; before that first navigation canGoBack() is false, AppPlugin re-dispatches and Back works, which is why this read as intermittent. SafeBackPlugin now claims ownership from its own constructor and again from load(), both strictly later than every plugin registered so far. The frontend semantic regression is blocking and green. The native WebView instrumentation remains in the Android runtime job but is explicitly quarantined after the 2026-08-22 two-attempt stop-loss: on GitHub's software-graphics emulator the process aborts before any JUnit assertion with Android libc reporting pthread_mutex_lock on a destroyed mutex. Managed-storage activation/crash-recovery tests run in a separate instrumentation lifetime and remain fully blocking.

entries.title: The tab close control stays pinned to the tab's right edge at any width and is a keyboard-operable button with its own Close tab tooltip

tests: src/components/TabBar.test.tsx::TabBar close control (GH #340)::is a real button with its own Close tab name, not the tab's pin tooltip

entries.notes: GH #340: a short title sized the tab near its 112px minimum but the close control sat directly after the text instead of at the tab's right edge, inviting accidental closes, and hovering it showed the inherited tab tooltip ('Double-click to pin (sticky)') instead of anything about closing. Both were layout/semantics only: the title now absorbs the tab's free space (flex: 1 1 auto with min-width: 0, so long titles still ellipsize) and the control is a real <button type=button> with an explicit title/aria-label 'Close tab'. Pointer-drag exemption, middle-click close, pinning and the last-tab guard are unchanged, and keyboard focus reveals the ✕ like hover does. jsdom cannot see the layout half, so that half was verified numerically in headless Chromium (closeRight == tabRight - 10px padding, titleRight == closeLeft - 6px gap, on both the Journals tab and a short-titled 'Tine' tab); screenshot eyeballing was unavailable in this worker session (no image input).

entries.title: Clicking empty main content then pressing a key paints no default focus frame around the page, while the deliberate pane-select ring survives
entries.notes: GH #345: the pane scroller `<main class=main-content tabindex=-1>` is a programmatic scroll/focus target; a click on empty page space focuses it, and the next keypress flips the UA's focus-visible heuristic so the browser paints its default frame (white on Windows WebView2/WebKitGTK) around the whole content area. Reproduced literally in headless Chromium pre-fix: click -> matchesFocus true, focusVisible false, outlineStyle none; keypress -> focusVisible true, outlineStyle auto 1px. Post-fix the same run leaves focus semantics intact (still focusable, still :matches(:focus-visible)) with outlineStyle none. The suppression is `.main-content:focus { outline: none }` only: the deliberate pane-select ring (`.pane-selected`, separate elements) is pinned by the style contract test, and actionable controls keep their own :focus-visible cues. The reporter's second repro (leaving pane-select with Esc after clicking the content) is the same focused-scroller mechanism and is covered by the same rule.

entries.title: Desktop Settings grows to a near-viewport dialog from a transient maximize/restore control, preserving page and scroll, while narrow viewports keep their full sheet without the control
entries.notes: GH #287 asked for a way to enlarge the Settings dialog (reporter: wasted space in long scroll views; 90% is fine). The desktop dialog gains a transient maximize/restore button in the pane head (inline SVG window glyphs, aria-pressed, labelled 'Maximize settings' / 'Restore settings size'). Geometry: the overlay trades its 12vh top gap for an even 4vh/4vw margin and the dialog fills it (~92vw x 92vh), all desktop-gated in @media (min-width: 481px) so a maximized-then-narrowed window can never break the mobile sheet's status-bar inset padding; <=480px keeps its existing full-viewport sheet and hides the control. The toggle is a pure class flip, so the selected settings page and scroll position ride through; the state resets on close (does not persist across modal reopen or restart). Verified numerically in headless Chromium: default 840x630 at (300,108) -> maximized 1325x828 at (58,36) on a 1440x900 viewport, active page 'Editor' retained across the toggle, reopen restores 840x630; mobile 390x844 shows display:none on the control and the unchanged 374x836 sheet. Scroll preservation asserted at render layer (scrollTop 120 survives both toggles); in the Chromium run the Editor pane simply clamped to its 38px max scroll at that width.

entries.title: A committed calculator block renders no phantom empty line for the fenced block's trailing newline, and no rows at all when fully blank
entries.notes: GH #339: while editing, the calc panel shows the correct number of lines, but after committing, the rendered CalcBlock showed one extra empty line. The parsed AST `code` of a fenced block ends with the newline before the closing fence, and evalCalc minted a row per split('\n') line, so the trailing '' became a phantom row. evalCalc now drops only TRAILING blank lines (LF/CRLF/whitespace-only) before mapping; interior blanks keep their row position, the all-blank block renders zero rows, and evaluation state is provably untouched (blank lines never modify env or `last`; row outputs are identical with and without trailing blanks). Both consumers share the function: the static CalcBlock and the editor's live results panel. The committed on-disk source is unchanged - this is render-only; no parser/round-trip involvement.

entries.title: Hiding the Android keyboard from the editor toolbar consumes the complete touch gesture; nothing underneath receives the trailing tap

tests: src/components/MobileKeyboardToolbar.test.tsx::consumes the full hide-keyboard gesture instead of touching through (GH #336)
src/components/MobileKeyboardToolbar.test.tsx::releases a cancelled hide-keyboard gesture after its safety window

entries.notes: GH #336: the Hide-keyboard button blurred the editor on pointerdown, which dropped the IME and unmounted the whole toolbar mid-gesture; Android then delivered the gesture's synthesized pointerup/click to whatever block sat behind it. The button now arms a short gesture window on pointerdown: the toolbar stays mounted and frozen at its pointer-down dock position while the IME-close resize grows the viewport, until the trailing click is consumed on the button itself; an AT/keyboard activation with no pointer gesture still blurs. A 700ms safety window retires cancelled or lost gestures. The lifecycle test simulates pointerdown -> blur -> IME-close resize -> trailing click and pins both mount lifetime and dock geometry. Physical Android confirmation remains a manager smoke-test item.

entries.title: Move Tab to pane {left,right,up,down} with no pane in that direction grows the layout: a multi-tab source donates its active tab into a new pane on that side; a one-tab source opens the new pane as a mirror of the current tab/history and stays intact

src/panes.test.ts::moveActiveTabInDirection (GH #282)::places the spawned pane before the source for left/up and after it for down

Previously the command no-op'ed whenever no pane lay in the direction — including the reporter's one-pane starting case, which needs it most. The new panes.ts moveActiveTabInDirection keeps the existing definite-move path when a neighbor exists (including the deliberate refusal to move a feed pane's lone journals tab), and otherwise splits the source in the requested direction: a multi-tab source donates only its active tab (moveTabToSplitPane), while a one-tab source — which Tine cannot empty — gets the same plain mirror split as pane-select Enter (splitSnapshotForNewPane semantics, including the journals-duplicate redirect to a selected feed day). New pane is focused, session save stays on the existing scheduleSessionSave boundary, and the mod+alt+shift+arrow bindings now call the shared function without the old layoutHasMultiplePanes() gate. Verified in vitest (7 new pane-layout cases across all four directions, one-tab/multi-tab/journals states, and the row-layout other-axis split); unit level only — not yet exercised in a native WebKit session.

entries.title: Toggle maximize active pane lends the focused pane the whole pane area transiently, restores the exact split tree and ratios on toggle, and falls back safely when the maximized pane closes or focus moves elsewhere

tests: src/panes.test.ts::pane maximize (GH #285)::shows only the maximized pane while keeping the real tree and ratios untouched
src/panes.test.ts::pane maximize (GH #285)::keeps mutations made while maximized, restoring the evolved tree exactly
src/panes.test.ts::pane maximize (GH #285)::clears when the maximized pane disappears, showing the surviving tree
src/panes.test.ts::pane maximize (GH #285)::restores the full layout when focus escapes to another pane
src/panes.test.ts::pane maximize (GH #285)::restores the full layout through the shared focus-state boundary

entries.notes: GH #285 minimal accepted design only: one remappable global command 'Toggle maximize active pane' (pane/toggle-maximize, default mod+alt+m, command-palette discoverable). Implementation is a pure view derivation, not a layout mutation: a transient maximizedPaneId signal makes visibleLayoutNode() return the single maximized leaf for the pane area, while layoutRoot() keeps the complete split tree and ratios, so nothing transient is serialized and toggling restores the exact arrangement including mutations made meanwhile. Safety: commitLayout() clears the state when the maximized pane disappears; the shared setFocusedPaneId state boundary unmaximizes when focus moves so history/session adapters cannot logically focus a hidden pane; resetPaneLayoutToSingle clears it. Deliberately out of scope: hidden-pane stacks, per-pane 1-9 commands, a persistent chrome button, and pane-select overlay rescaling while maximized. entries.title: Clicking a loaded Direct Files block's bullet enters that exact block without re-reading or replacing its page
entries.notes: GH #354 (Windows 11, Direct Files, v0.6.93): clicking a block bullet stamps a missing durable id and starts its guarded save before navigating to the block route. The route loader then re-read the same file's pre-save bytes and treated them as a competing page instance, producing the misleading unsaved-changes/other-file refusal. PageView now reuses only a block zoom's already-loaded exact path-aware owner. Component coverage drives the literal bullet click while its durable-id save is pending and proves no second read or refusal, then covers transient-live/durable identity resolution, restored-route disk loading when the owner is absent, and fail-closed handling of a different same-name physical owner.
